lede: The biggest thing on the board this week is the Carhenge redevelopment at 700 W Pacific Ave, where HARC holds three separate Preliminary Large-Scale public hearings Tuesday on Buildings A through E across Lots 34 and 34B of Backman Village — new construction in an Accommodations 2 zone, and the kind of project that will reshape that corner of town for a long time. Also Tuesday, the County Commissioners take up two Land Use Code amendments, including updated rules for Natural Medicine Businesses and Nonconforming Lots, both of which have real implications for what gets built and operated in San Miguel County. And if you want some fresh air with a purpose, the Open Space Commission's Valley Floor weed pull on Sunday at Eider Creek Trailhead includes an open public comment period.
